Over a decade after Boy Meets World ended in 2000, a spinoff series was developed for Disney Channel and called Girl Meets World. But even after Girl ended in 2017, there were still some characters that fans wanted to see more of. That’s all the more reason I'm so excited to hear Will Friedle and Matthew Lawrence talking about their own spinoff idea. And, seriously, I need a network exec to hear them out!

Cory Matthews and Shawn Hunter may have been one of the most perfect best friend pairings, based on their exploits in Boy Meets World. However, those two characters' older brothers, Jack and Eric, are also truly a bromance deserving of attention. During a recent episode of Pod Meets World, Matthew Lawrence, who played Jack, said during a press junket that he was asked about a Jack/Eric spin-off series. Will Friedle dropped some very positive thoughts on the prospect, and they make me giddy:

I think you could still do it. Jack and Eric come together. It’s the new Odd Couple!

Yes! This needs to come together. For those who don’t know, Neil Simon’s play The Odd Couple is about two mismatched roommates, and Jack and Eric definitely fit that bill. While Jack is the logical straight man of the duo, Eric is the zany eccentric. As the two characters (and the actors who played) were so yin and yang, a spinoff would definitely make for some entertaining TV.

Lawrence went on to explain that a Jack/Eric spinoff was once in the cards, but the relationship between the creators and Disney “kind of fell apart.” Also, Lawrence recently told EW he could see the duo, both in their 40s, forced back together after going their separate ways. Lawrence continued to say on the podcast that if a potential spinoff isn’t picked up by television, he has an excellent idea of how a micro spin-off series could work, and I’m loving it:

If anything, it’s like the new YouTube in a sense that these days, as you see with Obsession and all of these things that are coming, I mean, that’s kind of the new groundlings when you talk about comedy. The new spot where they bring out shows. So maybe if we even start, maybe it’s like, build it and they will come.

It’s true that YouTube has become the new platform for creatives to bring their ideas to fruition before they hit the big or small screens. If there's enough attention, it would be so interesting to see if this possible BMW offshoot could hit streaming one day.

Friedle said himself he’s “totally down” for a spinoff, so I'm feeling somewhat hopeful that the two might try to see this through. The last time fans saw Jack’s big one-time return on Girl Meets World, he reunited with Eric. However, it was revealed that Jack was a high-ranking executive at an environmentally harmful firm, which clashed with Eric's position as a newly elected senator. However, the iconic duo mended fences at Eric’s niece’s school dance, with Jack admitting that his friendship with his old pal was “the best choice” he ever made.

This TV show idea seems better than a previously proposed spin-off idea that came while Boy Meets World was still airing. Friedle revealed he almost left the ABC/Disney sitcom when creator Michael Jacobs pitched a “young Friends” idea for Eric to move to L.A. and meet new friends there. While it’s always amusing to see Eric’s humorous interactions, I’d rather see a straight man/funny man dynamic between him and Jack.

Now that the idea of a Jack/Eric spinoff has been brought up, this Boy Meets World fan is keeping her fingers crossed that it comes to fruition. Given that mismatched roommate shows like The Big Bang Theory, 2 Broke Girls, Perfect Strangers have been successful, why not give Jack Hunter and Eric Matthews a shot?

In the meantime, fans can watch Eric and Jack's dynamic on Boy Meets World and Girl Meets World by streaming them with a Disney+ subscription.

#3790. Activision cracking down on popular Call of Duty: Warzone app that basically constituted cheating

"Lobby shopping" is what Call of Duty: Warzone players have been calling the ability to check the skill level of players in a lobby prior to joining it, enabling them to pass on those that include a lot of tough competition.

There are several ways players, notably Twitch streamers and content creators, have been able to do that over the years. But the use of one app in particular - Warzone Agent - has been considered by many to be cheating, and Activision is finally doing something about it.

Alongside the launch of Modern Warfare 4's version of Warzone and the game's first season of post-launch content, Call of Duty's anti-cheat team Ricochet has announced it's officially cracking down on Warzone Agent.

"Yesterday, we began taking action against Warzone Agent, a paid, unauthorised third party tool that lets users lobby shop in Warzone," the developer revealed in a post on X. "Ricochet anti-cheat will block players attempting to load the software and instruct them to unload it before accessing multiplayer."

Having the ability to cherrypick the lobby with the lowest-skilled players possible bypasses the game's matchmaking algorithm, potentially ruining the game for the dozens of other players in the match. Historically, content creators have used the app (and other methods) to post impressive kill records.

The developer added in a follow-up message that: "Using unauthorised software to manipulate the player experience violates Activision terms of use and leaves your account and hardware subject to enforcement." The language seems to stop just short of outright confirming those players using Warzone Agent will be banned.

As part of this crackdown, Ricochet reiterated its stance on boosting - artificially increasing (or decreasing) one's skill rating - saying that it too is considered cheating. "Receiving a boost, having another player log in to boost your account, or purchasing a boosted account are all against policy," the developer said.

"Boosting services flood lobbies with low effort accounts used to farm XP and complete challenges. Those accounts can later be sold as Ranked Play ready, directly feeding the cheating marketplace."

More than 20,000 boosting-related accounts have been removed since the launch of Modern Warfare 4, according to the developer, and Ricochet will "continue to apply pressure" in this area.

The quality of multiplayer was a particular highlight in Eurogamer's review of Modern Warfare 4, in which Dom Peppiatt lauded the complexity of weapon handling, which works without taking away from accessibility of the gunplay.

#3789. Complete DREADMOOR Walkthrough: Part 1

DREADMOOR is now out in early access, and it presents an interesting tale for you to explore. Set in a dark, murky world, you have to capture different fish, explore locations, and upgrade your boat.

The campaign of DREADMOOR begins with a tentacle knocking you in the water. The story is broken into multiple quests that you can complete.

The opening will lead you to safe piece of land, and your main objective to get your boat. To do so, you’ll have to power up the generator with the fuel. Once you reach the generator, go to the hut right from there. You’ll find the fuel to power up the generator.

Once the generator has been powered up, you’ll unlock the boat, and then start exploring the world of DREADMOOR. Make sure to pick up the Hook Gun as well along the way.

First, we have to head to the Church Settlement. This place will provide you with your first weapon that allows you to clear blockages. Moreover, you’ll also find the first bed where you can sleep for the night to be over.

Next, we set sail for the Trading Post. Here, we will meet the trader and he will task us with some quest. The trader will also provide us with different blueprints to purchase, but that’s something you can ignore for now.

From there, go upwards to patch the hole in the wall in your shelter. Here, you’ll find the Simple Rod, and you can now fish in the waters. But first, sleep on the bed to survive the night.

Once we get the fishing rod, the next task is to open the door to the Dry Dock. Get the required resources, and then speak with the Engineer to open the doors. This will then allow you to clean and upgrade your ship.

Before you can install the upgrades, you’ll also need to clean the polyps from your ship using the water pipe. Then, you can install the upgrades after crafting them with the required resources. To do so, you’ll have to unlock the blueprints first.

This will complete the first part of the game and get you up to date with all the basics.

I can't remember the last time I just went on an adventure in an MMO.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

World of Warcraft: Forever's quests are kind of a pain in the ass—they are this way because of the archaic, pre-solved quest design of the early 2000s (which is still very much more convenient than the MMOs that came before it). But it's also somewhat deliberate.

Back then, forcing you to run halfway across the map to talk to some dude halfway up a mountain (or in the example I'll talk about later on, a fight pit on an island somewhere) was a way to get you out in the world, exploring it, originally unfolding new questing hubs or putting new flight routes and settlements in front of you.

Over time, that design fell by the wayside in favor of convenience. The prospect of having to go out of your way for something that wasn't a strictly superior source of XP became a 'waste of time'. And to some degree, I get it. If you're worried about efficiency, having to jog for five minutes might feel like a chore.

Besides, WoW's always been a game that people are rushing to solve, and I think that's just grand—solving puzzles is fun. I am the kind of person to cheer on speedrunners, to be fascinated by optimisation. People are clever and determined and they will find unique and novel ways to push the envelope.

But boy, am I glad I'm not listening to them.

Quest helping addons have been a point of contention since Forever's launch—partially because some of them are paid services—and while I'm not going to comment on the meta-drama, I will say that, from an experiential point of view, avoiding them was the right choice for me.

That's not to say I've simply been bumbling about. I've been looking at the quests that land in my log and trying to figure out the most efficient way to get through them; and I'm at what I think is a respectable level 32 after around 52 hours /played (a number I've only hit because I am playing this game as part of my job).

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

I'm also not a complete vegan. I'm using the modernised in-game quest map marker, like some kind of oldschool pescatarian—though I will say that we did have these back in vanilla. They're just part of the UI, now.

But I've also not been sweating the small stuff. Did I do a quest chain in an order that means I've gotta hoof it back across Darkshire? Sure. Did I miss a dungeon quest? Cool, whatever. I'll either come back to it later or just not do the quest. I have free will and an "abandon quest" button.

And, more to the point, I've occasionally been taking holidays from that efficiency to go and do stuff that's way out there. For instance, the "Fire Hardened Mail" warrior questline, which sent my alliance character all the way to goddamn Razorfen Kraul in the Southern Barrens.

While there, I met an incredibly chill group of fellow allies who informed me there was a quest a little ways into Thousand Needles and, together, we hopped down the lift, grabbed a book, nattered a touch, ran away from centaurs, and then—like, 40 minutes later—finally got into the dungeon, where I tanked the whole thing as Fury because pickings were slim and nobody in their right mind would've made this trek.

Another warrior questline—this one mandatory—asks you to take the hike from Theramore all the way up to an island off the coast of Ratchet. And it's here that the Forever of it all kicked in, and those hand-crafted, zone-specific weather effects and lighting tricks instilled such a deep feeling of zen in me.

It was pouring it down with rain as I jogged up the beach from Theramore. I had to dodge a bunch of murlocs on their islands, snagged a few ore deposits on the way, and swam through stormy, turbulent seas to the Barrens' coastline. When I got there, it was sunset and considerably less rainy, so I jogged through the shallow waters to Fray Island just as the sun kissed the ocean.

And hey, it turns out that this time, I did actually more-or-less take the most efficient route—but this questline, a mandatory class quest to get all your stances, has a lot of experiences like it mirrored in other quests that are actually off the beaten path.

The actual Fray questline isn't anything special. On paper, it's just a "stand in a spot and beat a few mooks to get your stance". But the fact I had to do all of that nonsense made it memorable. Similarly, while my Fire Hardened Hauberk is a pretty nice blue, it was objectively not worth my time to do the long, arduous quest to get it. And yet, I had a great adventure anyway.

And it got me thinking: When was the last time I had an adventure in WoW? Not a quest, not a delve, not a seasonal track, but an actual honest-to-god adventure? One I chose to engage with, one that required me to think about how best to get to some far-flung place, one that required me to talk with other players (the horror), and one that—more importantly—took a lot of time I could've used elsewhere?

For some players, that whole journey is replaced with an arrow, or a 'do this next' prompt. And I'm not saying you can't enjoy the game in that way. For some, efficiency is a sport, and they should get to play ball. But boy did I make the right move for my own personal enjoyment, and I'd recommend that if you're feeling a little pale around the gills about questing to unplug and do the same.

#3787. Rockstar's doing a GTA 6 launch 'festival' in Miami featuring a lot of presumably expensive musical stars

The next-level glamour of Grand Theft Auto 6's arrival continues with word that Rockstar is hosting a star-studded launch 'festival' for the game in Miami - the game's setting-by-a-different-name.

The event will feature two stages hosting live performances by musical artists both featured in the game and from those who are not. Cardi B is probably the headliner - my knowledge of popular music is creaking here - but there's also Travis Scott, Don Toliver, Kodak Black, Sofaygo, Ca7riel, and Paco Amoroso.

Meanwhile, GTA 6 soundtrack duo Justice are doing a DJ set, as are The Dare with Fcukers, which is a dangerous name to spell. Also appearing: Metro Boomin, Nick León with DJ Python, Propsa with Skream, Rauw and Friends, Suero, and Tainy.

The event is being hosted at event space Mana Wynwood, and the pre-sale lottery for tickets begins this week on Wednesday, 11th November. Tickets are limited to two a head.

The full soundtrack for GTA 6 is yet to be revealed, with only a handful of songs so far detailed - featuring Rauw, Ca7riel, Paco Amoroso, and Travis Scott, among others. But of course music and radio stations play a huge role in the series, and given the amount of time we'll be playing GTA 6 and listening to these songs, it may well provide a lucrative platform to be featured on.

Meanwhile, the cultural impact of GTA 6's imminent arrival continues with a takeover of swanky department store Selfridges in London, which has a custom Ferrari parked in a window and an extensive range of expensive merch to buy.

It's not all good news for Rockstar, though. The company is also fighting an employment tribunal in Scotland relating to the sudden firing of 31 staff from Rockstar North this time last year. Rockstar alleges this was done for gross misconduct reasons, whereas the fired staff maintain it was done in the name of union busting. The results of that hearing are expected close to GTA 6's release, on 19th November.

Here's everything you need to do to get inside the Crimson Manor in Phantom Blade Zero

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Opening the Phantom Blade Zero Crimson Manor is a long and difficult process that you won't complete until you're very far into the game – basically, if you're reading this because you've just stumbled upon the manor under the Weeping Creek Valley Sha-Chi Tower, don’t worry about it for now!What makes it so complicated is that getting the necessary tongue key ties into several other side quests that will take you all over the game world, and the Crimson Manor quest itself links to an even greater over-arching side quest. But, to help you out, I've explained the entire process of getting inside the Crimson Manor – be aware that there are some story spoilers below!

To get inside the Crimson Manor, you need to get the Puppet's Tongue key by going through three hidden portal doors found across the game, all of which lead to the Three-Eyed Puppet (this is 'The Herald's Illusion' quest).

The arduous part is therefore finding those doors, especially since two of them are in far-flung regions of the game, so you need to make sure you have access to those regions first. To reach the Mandate Encampment, you need the Phantom Blade Zero Mandate Encampment Key. And to get to the Mountain of Imprisonment, you must have repaired the Illusory Pipa, which you can only do if you have found Myst in Pangzhen and thoroughly explored the Village of Lu, the Mandate Encampment, and Meigu Lake for the missing parts.

With all that in mind, here are the locations of the three secret doors:

When you go through the final door, interact with the Three-Eyed Puppet and it'll give you the necessary Puppet's Tongue, completing 'The Herald's Illusion' quest in the process, and finally giving you access to this mysterious subterranean mansion. The puppet also hands over its own Yin blue crystal eye and says that you need to find the Yang eye within the Crimson Manor, which is all for the 'Secrets at the Heart of the Lake' quest.

Anyway, fast travel to the Crimson Manor and interact with the lock to insert the tongue and open the door. Plunder the manor then head out the back and jump down the pit, carefully working your way to the bottom.

You'll be faced with a double boss fight against the Puppet Scavenger and Acolyte Hansui here. Neither are that tough, with the former's huge bulk making it slow and easy to hit and the latter being quite easy to overwhelm up close, so long as you dodge and block plenty of their ice attacks. Kill the pair and you'll get the Yang eye and Hansui's Frost Mask, thus finally completing the Crimson Manor quest!But now you've got the Yin and Yang crystal eyes and the 'Secrets at the Heart of the Lake' quest to wrap up. If you haven't already, you need to defeat the other three Acolyte boss fights found at scarecrows around the game – there's one in the Village of Lu, Pangzhen, and Lake Meigu – and take their masks to the Four Guardians' Mirror on the icy western side of Lake Meigu. This will take you to a special area where you'll eventually get to use those two crystal eyes, but only after you defeat the Blizzard Blademaster.

You've got to spend quite a lot of time in the Mandate Encampment for this quest, so make sure you grab Moji's House Key in Phantom Blade Zero while you're there. You'll also be facing a lot of bosses along the way, and it helps to have the best Phantom Blade Zero Accessories equipped.

#3784. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang under investigation after admitting affair with alleged Chinese spy in company-wide email

"There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry."

Nvidia's board of directors has launched an investigation into its own CEO Jensen Huang, after a report by the New York Times claimed he had been participating in an affair with an alleged Chinese spy.

Huang admitted to having an affair in a company-wide statement, apologising to his wife as well as to Nvidia employees. Following this acknowledgement, independent investigators are looking into whether or not he's been the target of a "foreign intelligence effort".

Per the New York Times article, the alleged spy was named as Megaspeed executive and Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang or Huang Le. Jensen Huang wrote in his internal letter: "I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry."

With regard to security concerns surrounding the CEO of US-based company Nvidia potentially sharing information with a spy, Huang confirmed that the Nvidia board of directors had initiated an investigation. He added: "I support the investigation and will cooperate fully." The Nvidia board has said it has "no reason to believe either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised."

Huang will remain CEO of Nvidia while the investigation is conducted. The New York Times report also claimed that US government officials did not believe Huang knew of Alice Huang's alleged intelligence activities for China.

Following the internal letter from Jensen Huang, Nvidia stock took a tumble from $162bn to $150bn. Nvidia, a juggernaut in the video game hardware industry, is also a key player in the global generative AI industry, which is currently carrying the US economy as other sectors struggle. The company is responsible for AI technology like DLSS 5, which generates lighting, shadows and more using generative AI.

Concerns around the Chinese AI sector passing the American industry has been a core argument against AI development slowdown or regulation, and it's also why Huang's affair may be a matter of national interest.

90 Day Fiancé: The Other Way finally showed Andi Wallace and Nigel having a heart-to-heart about boundaries in their relationship, and I think it unintentionally revealed why this relationship may never work. Andi is ready for a relationship with a deep emotional connection, and it doesn't seem like Nigel is willing to do that.

TLC teased the first part of Nigel and Andi's conversation ahead of the episode, but now that we have the full context, I have thoughts. Can Nigel really be jealous of Andi texting other men, when he's seemingly unwilling to offer her anything different than what he does with all his lovers? Let's talk this out.

The latest episode of 90 Day Fiancé: The Other Way to air amid the 2026 TV schedule brought up something that I'm not even sure Andi realized in the moment. While Nigel went after her for texting other men, he defended his relationships with other women as they were purely physical with limited to zero texting beyond that. Minutes later, Andi mentioned that he wouldn't text her when he's with other women, and Nigel argued that he would rarely text anyone, period.

I personally found that exchange to be telling. Since the start, I've had trouble figuring out how Nigel's relationship with Andi is different than any of his other part-time lovers. Based on their conversation about texting, I'm beginning to get the feeling that it isn't, which feels like a major problem.

90 Day Fiancé: The Other Way fans are still on the fence about whether Andi or Nigel are still together at this point. That's been even more uncertain since the revelation that Andi had been on Tinder and was embracing her side of ethical non-monogamy.

90 Day Fiancé's Angela Deem Drops Cryptic Message About Michael When Asked About Hunt For Love

I'm now wondering if the reason their relationship feels so ambiguous is due to Nigel treating Andi like she's a part-time lover. To be fair, if she ended up returning to the United States like some believe, that feels like a part-time romance. Is Nigel wrong for treating someone that way when he can only roam grocery stores with them barefoot once in a blue moon?

Also, I wouldn't be surprised if Andi realized she just wasn't going to get the emotional connection from Nigel that she desperately craved. It doesn't sound like his part-time lovers are getting that treatment either, which could just mean that it's not something he's ever going to give a partner. These two just may be a bad match, but we'll just have to wait and see.

#3782. How to check how many chests you’ve opened in Fortnite Treasure Hunters

Looting is more important than ever before in Fortnite’s Treasure Hunters mini-season, as there are lots of freebies up for grabs this time around, including access to everything in the shop if you get really lucky. Because of this, you may be searching for a way to keep track of how many chests you’ve opened.

Finding and opening chests is the only way to get your hands on quite a few rare items this season, so keeping an eye on all of the work you’ve put in is a helpful tool for tracking progress. It can be tricky to find on your own, though, so here’s how to check how many chests you’ve opened in Fortnite.

You can keep track of how many chests you’ve opened in Fortnite Treasure Hunters from the Quests tab. This helpful mechanic can be easy to miss, as there are quite a lot of missions to tackle listed in this section. Here’s how to find it.

Each of the chest quests listed here tracks your progress across five stages. As you hit each of the five milestones for these bonus goals, you earn extra XP, and the listed maximum number of chests being tracked increases.

These missions only track chests up to 1,000 for each type, so once you hit this number in each of the three categories, your total opened chests will no longer be displayed. This means you can only check your opened chests for the season up until you hit this cap.

Read what’s behind the latest news in gaming (with a bit of snark) by subscribing to the Destructoid Checkpoint newsletter!

The number of chests you open does not directly affect your odds of finding the Pirate Shop Access or other special loot drop items. The loot odds and drop rates are completely unrelated to how many chests you open, as this system is completely based on RNG, which means it comes down to random luck and chance.

Although opening more chests doesn’t directly increase your odds of finding Pirate Shop Access and other loot items, the more you loot, the more shots you have at potentially finding something. This system can be a bit confusing to fully understand, but a good way to conceptualize it is to compare the loot system to a bag of marbles.

Think of all the special loot items as rare, colored marbles in a big bag of grey ones. Each time you open a chest, you’re pulling a marble out. If the marble is grey, it goes right back in. If it’s colored, it stays out.

Your odds of pulling a colored one, which is a special loot item, don’t increase over time, as the grey marbles, or standard loot items, always go back into the pool. At the same time, the more you reach into the bag by opening chests, the more shots you have at finding items.

Although you can’t boost your odds of finding rare drops by opening more chests, you can help the process along by attending special events that feature boosted odds for these rare items. Treasure Hours are the best time to go looting for these assets.

#3781. Anticipated Warhammer 40K tactical RPG Dark Heresy gets a release date

Owlcat Games has revealed a release date for its tactical role-playing sequel Warhammer 40,000: Dark Heresy. The game arrives 28th January, 2027 on PC, PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series S/X. A Switch 2 release date will be provided "at a later date", a press release says.

Warhammer 40,000: Dark Heresy follows the good work laid down by Warhammer 40,000: Rogue Trader a couple of years ago. "Rogue Trader nails the 40k setting and provides an appropriately massive narrative filled with meaty tactical combat, though some bugs and poor performance hold it back," wrote Caeyln Ellis in Eurogamer's Warhammer 40,000 Rogue Trade review.

Dark Heresy changes things by casting you as an Inquisitor and tasking you with hunting down heretics and purging the world of dark influences, as one is wont to do in the 41st century, it seems. And developer Owlcat has apparently overhauled many of the systems underpinning the adventure.

There's a beta that's been running for a while that offers a complete first Act to try, and it's accessible if you buy a Founders edition of the game. This beta, incidentally, disappears 7th January, when Owlcat prepares the game for launch.

Meanwhile, Owlcat is making a substantially different RPG based around the popular Expanse license - a game that's much more closely inspired by Mass Effect. That project recently recruited the help of former Dragon Age writer David Gaider, and it will no doubt hope to fill a much-lamented hole created recently by the cancellation of Mass Effect 5.

Tickets will be available via a lottery system for those aged 17+ with exclusive codes being sent out to those who managed to win a spot when the entries are drawn on today at 4 pm ET/ 9 pm GMT. But there are a couple things to keep in mind. There's no word on how expensive the tickets will be, with prices likely being revealed later today in the lottery, and the festival is a mere two weeks away, as it takes place on November 21, 2026.

So, unless you're a super fan with money to spare on not only a festival ticket but also a last-minute plane ticket to Miami, this event will likely be for locals or, at the very least, those already in the US. My only issue is that if you're so big a fan that you're willing to drop everything last minute and head over to Florida then why aren't you actually playing GTA 6? The festival is happening just two days after GTA 6, I'm pretty sure we're all busy around then.

Writer and director Martin McDonagh's latest movie, Wild Horse Nine, had a triumphant run across film festival season before landing in theaters nationwide this weekend on the 2026 movie schedule. I’ve been excited to see it since I first saw the trailer, or really, since I heard the movie was getting made. I’m a big fan of most of McDonagh's work, and the cast includes some of my favorites, like John Malkovich, Sam Rockwell, Steve Buscemi, and Parker Posey. And there is a lot to love about the film. However, I can’t shake the feeling that I really didn’t care about Chris (Malkovich) and his fate, and that makes it hard to think of Wild Horse Nine as one of the best movies of the year.

As with some of McDonagh's other high water marks, specifically In Bruges and The Banshees of Inisherin, Wild Horse Nine brings what I appreciate most about his work: a dysfunctional friendship. It’s that friendship and the banter between Chris and Lee (Rockwell) that I love about the movie. The dialogue is crisp, biting, and hilarious. It’s also touching. They don’t hate each other like the characters in the other two movies I mention. They love and respect each other. They trust each other with their lives (literally).

I also love the ridiculous premise of the movie and the over-the-top nature of it. Chris was JFK’s assassin, for example. Often I would hate that kind of plot point, but here, it’s just ridiculous enough to make sense. I also love that most of the movie takes place in an exotic location. Easter Island is a unique place, and you don’t often see movies set there. Every time there is a giant moai in the background or a wild horse (though they have nothing to do with the title, apparently) on the road, it adds to the surrealness of it all. I loved all that.

Chris is dying. He’s got cancer, and he is dealing with dementia. He knows he’s not long for the world and decides he’s going to go out on his terms, with an assist from his loyal partner, protege, and friend, Lee. Lee, meanwhile, is working with their boss, MJ (Buscemi), to take Chris out anyway. This is the heart of the movie, the motivation that keeps Lee and Chris going, but I, frankly, didn’t care.

That might sound cold-hearted, but I didn’t. I didn’t feel an emotional attachment to what should have been the emotional center of the movie. I almost feel bad saying this, but despite the great dialogue and the cool setting, the movie didn’t move me at all. It all just passed over me like a “good hang” rather than a film that tugged at me. It felt empty to me in that respect.

Wild Horse Nine is going to get a ton of attention come award season, and let me say that I am all in on Malkovich getting nominated and finally winning a long-deserved Oscar for his work here. I hope McDonagh is nominated for best director, too. I certainly hope Rockwell gets his flowers as well. However, this isn’t the best movie I’ve seen this year, and I’ll likely be pulling for another movie come Oscar time.

#3777. Hollow Knight Silksong physical editions mention multiple "free content packs" incoming, and call Sea of Sorrow a "giant expansion"

More than a year after its initial release, physical versions of Hollow Knight: Silksong are finally arriving on players' doorsteps. It's the same brilliant and sometimes thrillingly cruel Metroidvania Eurogamer gave five stars to, except this time a pack-in booklet seemingly reveals the existence of multiple "free content packs" alongside the Sea of Sorrow DLC.

Hollow Knight: Silksong's physical editions were originally set to be delivered from 10th November, but some early handovers have given us a peek inside the box. Redditor Me_975 posted pictures of their Nintendo Switch 2 Edition, and there's a few interesting tidbits tucked away - most notably in the manual's chapter on Content Packs.

"The world of Hollow Knight: Silksong will expand with free content packs," the booklet reads. "Prepare for even more adventures filled with new friends, new abilities, and new ferocious foes!"

Developer Team Cherry confirmed plans for post-launch Silksong support last year, but remained pretty tight-lipped about what exactly that would look like. The indie outfit then announced the nautically themed Sea of Sorrow expansion, though we now have proper confirmation there's more content packs still to come, which shouldn't be a huge shocker considering all the free post-launch love Hollow Knight (the first one) received.

Speaking of Sea of Sorrow, that's mentioned here too: "In the first giant expansion, voyage across and beneath a salt-stricken ocean brimming with mystery and menace."

Sea of Sorrow's original release window was a vague 2026 - time's a-ticking, Team Cherry. Still no release date so far, but the booklet does say it's "Coming Soon." Of course, Team Cherry are quite infamous for working on games until they balloon wildly out of control. After all, Silksong was once upon a time intended to be a Hollow Knight DLC, but with games this detailed, I can't really complain about waiting a little extra.

If you are interested in owning Silksong physically, it comes with a big map of Pharloom and the rest of the booklet also includes some really lovely art seemingly ripped straight from the game, as well.

Nvidia has found itself at the center of a spying scandal as its CEO, Jensen Huang, admitted to an affair with an alleged Chinese intelligence asset. A couple of hundred billion dollars have been wiped off the company's value and law firms are already circling for blood.

A handful of law firms have announced they are urging investors to sign up to cover their losses through legal action or initial investigations, including Rosen Law Firm and Schall, Brown & Schwartz. They say they're going after the company on charges of false and/or misleading statements and failure to disclose key information.

An official Nvidia spokesperson previously denied claims that Jensen Huang had anything beyond a normal relationship with Alice Huang, the alleged spy, at the end of October. The company also vouched for Megaspeed, the Singaporean datacentre company that Alice Huang has been connected with, saying that any claims of its involvement in chip smuggling have been "thoroughly investigated and debunked"; which Megaspeed reiterates on its website.

Since then, Huang has admitted his relationship with Alice Huang was not a normal business relationship. Alice Huang has also been noted as a Chinese intelligence asset by US authorities; something which a memo circulated around the Trump administration is reported to have said at a much earlier date.

Nvidia's board is also launching an investigation into whether Jensen Huang was the target of foreign intelligence. The board states that it has "no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised."

Who knew what and when is all set to be litigated one way or another, as Jensen Huang is heading to a closed-door meeting with Congress committee leaders to discuss his relationship with Alice Huang on November 18.

Further to that, president Donald Trump, speaking to reporters at the White House, briefly mentioned he believed the FBI to be "looking into" the matter. He also said he believed Huang to be an "honourable guy" and generally seemed to get behind the Nvidia CEO.

Any class action suit could take a very long time to resolve. There's still an open claim for a class action regarding Nvidia's actions during the cryptocurrency mining boom of 2017-18. Remember that? It sucked, too.

The 2020 case has been bouncing around the courts for a while now, being dismissed, revived, and sent up to the Supreme Court, before being sent back down again in 2024. Now, in 2026, they might just think about starting an actual trial—maybe. We're talking eight years after the actual events leading to the case.

#3775. How to dance on a driveable car in Fortnite Treasure Hunters

Weekly quests will have you attempting to check off all kinds of strange tasks in Fortnite. One of the weirder ones you’ll encounter in Treasure Hunters asks you to dance on a driveable car.

Quests like this one can be tough to complete, as you’re tasked with seeking out a specific item around the vast island. If you’re struggling to get this mission done, here’s how to dance on a driveable car in Fortnite.

A driveable car is any vehicle you can find and hop behind the wheel of around the Fortnite island. In Treasure Hunters, there are a few different types of cars you can find while exploring, including:

Read what’s behind the latest news in gaming (with a bit of snark) by subscribing to the Destructoid Checkpoint newsletter!

Drievable cars can be found all around the Fortnite island. Overall, though, they’re most commonly found sitting on roads and parked near main, named POIs. The tough part of finding these vehicles is that none of them are guaranteed to spawn in every round. There’s a chance you may encounter a driveable car while exploring around most areas on the island. Some of the overall best spots to check for them, though, are as follows.

To complete the dance on a driveable car quest in Fortnite, you need to locate a vehicle that can be driven, hop on top of it, and perform any dancing emote. As soon as you do, this quest will be complete.

#3774. God of War: Ragnarok is reportedly the highest-earning PlayStation Studios game this generation, but Marvel's Spider-Man 2 isn't far behind

God of War: Ragnarok is the generation's best-selling and highest-earning PlayStation Studios game, according to a new report, but the full top 10 list has a few nice surprises.

In the four years since its PS5 release and two years since its PC port, God of War: Ragnarok has reportedly sold just over 20m copies and generated $1.4b in revenue, according to estimates from Alinea Analytics. About 27.5 percent of the 15m copies it sold on console came from physical editions, and the action blockbuster apparently sold a further 1.1m this year alone. Not bad, boy.

Those stats should bode well for the series' next romp God of War: Laufey - which sees Faye take the spotlight across a multi-mythological afterlife and was recently delayed into May 2027 - even if PlayStation moves away from PC ports for its signature single-player games.

Kratos and Atreus only narrowly beat out perhaps the biggest superhero of them all: Marvel's Spider-Man 2, a game that reportedly made a whopping $1.3b off 19.1m copies across PS5 and PC. The Spidey sequel should keep swinging even higher as the years chug on, though - the report states that sales always surge during the holiday months, and this year's big screen behemoth Spider-Man: Brand New Day led to an even bigger spike than usual.

Racing sim royalty Gran Turismo 7 ($841m), bug-squashing phenomenon Helldivers 2 ($786m), robo-dino sequel Horizon: Forbidden West ($485m), vengeful spirit sim Ghost of Yotei ($410m), undead remake The Last of Us Part 1 ($341m), multidimensional romp Ratchet and Clank: Rift Apart ($334m), Stellar Blade ($316m) and delightful throwback Astro Bot ($292m) round out the top 10 games published by PlayStation Studios this generation.

It's worth noting that Helldivers 2 and Stellar Blade were developed by studios outside the PlayStation umbrella, but the console maker still published both upon release. Ghost of Yotei's performance is also particularly impressive since Sucker Punch's sequel has only been out for a year and didn't get the benefit of a PC port, like many of its PS5 siblings. The success couldn't save Sucker Punch from recent layoffs, however.

On PlayStation's decision to kill disc-based physical releases, analyst Rhys Elliott said that the bottom five games in the list together made $281.7m this year alone: "PlayStation wants those numbers to be bigger in the coming years, which is one of the reasons it's killing the disc (alongside the better margins it and publishers get through digital.)"

I'm Commander Shepard and this is my favorite video on the internet.

This N7 Day was the first without developer BioWare around, but fans of the Mass Effect series didn't let 7th November go by quietly. The community managed to get several notable Mass Effect actors to lend their voice to the increasingly loud 'SaveMassEffect' movement.

In the weeks since BioWare's shock closure and Mass Effect Universe's cancellation, the community-organised We Are Mass Effect group have put up billboards in Times Square, a mobile billboard outside BioWare Edmonton's former office and much more while directing attention to an online petition.

Today is a very special day for Mass Effect fans. We've worked incredibly hard to bring together most of the original Mass Effect trilogy's voice cast to share a very important message with you. We need to #SaveMassEffect. https://t.co/FOp0qp4wBI

And for the series' annual celebration, the group managed to get a sizable portion of the Mass Effect cast to join in. Commander Shepard actors Jennifer Hale and Mark Meer, original trilogy composer Sam Hulick, Garrus' Brandon Keener, Jack's Courtnay Taylor, Tali'Zorah's Ash Sroka, Thane's Keythe Farley and many more all showed up in a two-minute video to help potentially salvage the series - sometimes in character.

"When we heard about the formal closing of Boware, I felt weirdly hopeful," Hale said in a separate interview with IGN. "I can't explain it. I just got so weirdly hopeful. My first thought, of course, was for the devs and all the people. And then I just closed my eyes and crossed my fingers and I said, 'I feel something's possible. You know, something's really possible.'"

The other half of Commander Shepard, Mark Meer, noted that "this didn't all just happen in the last 10 days." Near yearly layoffs at EA had slowly trimmed multiple BioWare teams down, sometimes even affecting studio veterans who had been at the company for decades.

"A lot of senior writers within the last year or two were let go. People who had been there from the very beginning. Again, people who had built that company from the ground up, who built the bones of it, who made those games that had captured people so much right back from the 1990s," Meer said.

In what they describe as "just a proof of concept", one Redditor has gone further than your average custom looper to help keep their game room cool, by routing the liquid cooling in their gaming PC outside to a radiator sat in the cold winter air.

The setup involves slapping a Bykski water block on their Nvidia RTX 4070 Ti and direct-die cooling on the Intel Core Ultra 7 270K Plus using a Thermal Grizzly 1851 Mycro Pro water block, after de-lidding the CPU, of course.

The two blocks are hooked up to each other, and the custom loop can feed water through a radiator outside through holes in the wall when needed.

Part of the reason for doing all this, the Redditor claims, is that their room gets warm when they game:

"My room gets warm when I game and it's -4 outside. Free cooling right? The catch is if the water going into the PC gets too cold you get condensation on the parts, and water dripping on a 4070 Ti Super is not the vibe. So the whole thing is built around keeping the water cold, but not too cold."

"The pc loop runs like normal. When it needs extra cooling, the second pump sends some of the water out to the rad outside and back in.

"A Python script starts on startup and it connects to the Arduino, takes over from the Arduino's own auto mode, and it connects to HWi and Fancontrol so i get total control over the dynamics."

The PC Gamer Circuit Breaker newsletter breaks down the latest PC gaming tech, and finds you the best deals on the best products

Yep, that's right; the loop also involves a secondary computer system managing everything. Part of the calculations the Arduino boards handle involves keeping temperatures above the "dew point", ie, above the point at which a difference in temps might make condensation form on the electronics. Because, y'know, that thing about water and electricity not mixing.

Although part of this was to keep the gaming room cool, I'm sure another part was pushing these components for performance. And on this front, there are some great results, including keeping the GPU running around 48 °C under load and the CPU at 52 °C under load. While playing CS2, the GPU stays at 34 °C and the CPU stays between 45–50 °C.

Given this is just a "proof of concept", there's more to be achieved, and the Redditor says: "I'm coming for that number two spot in Steel Nomad for 4070 Ti Super." In other words, they're trying to beat out some top records for that 3DMark benchmark. Let's hope for a nice and chilly winter, then.

I've watched enough behind-the-scenes footage from Denis Villeneuve's book-to-screen adaptation of the Dune series to know making Arrakis convincing takes a lot of sand. But hearing Zendaya and Robert Pattinson describe what filming the final installment in the movie franchise was like has me reaching for a glass of ice water. Apparently, playing people who live on a desert planet involves wishing you weren't on one.

Zendaya and Pattinson joined their co-stars for a conversation with The New York Times about Villeneuve's trilogy finale, which arrives on the 2026 movie schedule in December. Zendaya, who reprised Chani for the film, said the blazing sun made acting with her face difficult. Between the heat and the early calls for makeup and prosthetics, it was anything but relaxing. As she tells it:

The hardest thing is to just meditate through the heat. There's scenes where the sun is so bright that I am trying to give another facial expression other than [Zendaya scrunches up her face as if in pain] and I physically can't. [Laughs] I was just pouring sweat, trying to focus, keep my eyes open as much as I can. You've got to get ready and set up before the sun starts coming up, while it's still cool, and also we had to get into the prosthetics of it all. No one earlier than Rob.

I Didn’t Expect Jason Momoa To Name Drop Disneyland While Describing Filming In The Desert For Dune 3

I'm sorry, but if the weather is physically preventing me from making facial expressions, I'm calling it a day. Seriously, I have enough trouble concentrating when the air conditioning goes out. Zendaya still has to convey Chani's complicated feelings about Paul Atreides while the sun tries to cook her through her costume.

Then there's Pattinson, who joins the franchise as Scytale. You'd think a newcomer might find the machinery overwhelming when it sounds like something from an amusement park. Instead, the actor seemed delighted by an elaborate sequence, explaining:

The desert is just another level. There's this one sequence where I'm in this spaceship, on a gimbal, on the edge of a sand dune, and we had this 350-foot-long model of a sandworm. The scale of this stuff is just unbelievable, you're having your own "Dune" theme park, where the gimbal is going upside down and flying, and this is not like work at all. There are no negatives.

A 350-foot sandworm model? I love details like that. Villeneuve could presumably leave plenty of the spectacle to visual effects, but building something that enormous gives the actors a very real piece of Arrakis to react to. Of course, Pattinson's declaration that there were "no negatives" came with a fairly disgusting exception. He continued:

Apart from having your sweat drained out of the top of your head, and getting like bulbous sweat bubbles. But even then, I didn't even really notice them. He's so easy to work with, Denis, it's never really a stress.

"Bulbous sweat bubbles" is an image I would have happily gone my entire life without imagining. Still, I appreciate how much he enjoyed working with Villeneuve, even if his body apparently found a brand-new way to perspire.

Dune: Part Three picks up nearly two decades after Paul's rise to power and concludes Villeneuve's adaptation of Frank Herbert's saga. It's due in theaters December 18, going head-to-head with Marvel’s Avengers: Doomsday. Judging by these cast stories from the making of Dune, the performers earned every minute we'll spend sitting comfortably in an air-conditioned auditorium. I'll gladly watch the sandworms, with my wildly themed popcorn bucket in hand, from the comfort of a reclined theater seat.

Ryan graduated from Missouri State University with a BA in English/Creative Writing. An expert in all things horror, Ryan enjoys covering a wide variety of topics. He's also a lifelong comic book fan and an avid watcher of Game of Thrones and House of the Dragon.

#3768. GTA 6 pre-orders are tracking "well above expectations" and the game will "set a new baseline" for Take-Two, says CEO Strauss Zelnick

Today, as part of Take-Two Interactive Software's Q2 2027 earnings call, Strauss Zelnick noted that pre-orders for Grand Theft Auto 6 are tracking "far above expectations", and is certain that soon "numbers will speak for themselves" when it comes to the game.

Zelnick also promised GTA Online and GTA 5 will continue to receive updates in order to support the "nearly 235 million" units sold to date across "an unprecedented three console generations". The GTA series as a whole has, to date, sold over 480 million units. Karl Statoff, president at Take-Two, adds the launch of GTA 6 will be a "defining moment for the company and global entertainment industry". Zelnick adds, later in a question and answer session, that he expects GTA 6 to "set a new baseline" for Take-Two. "The future's really bright across the board," he notes.

For the next quarter, Take-Two expects to deliver $3.35 billion to $3.5 billion - with "recurrent consumer spending" to raise by 12 percent, driven by "the groundbreaking release" of Grand Theft Auto 6, and expects to see "significant growth for the Grand Theft Auto series", driven by sales of - specifically - Grand Theft Auto 6's Ultimate Edition, which includes add-on content, and that most people are pre-ordering at its $100 price point. That bonus $20 between the $80 base edition and the Ultimate Edition is counted as "recurrent consumer spending", as is part of that massive bump the company has seen.

It also seems that we will see more GTA games - or content, at least - sooner than expected. "We do think that the nature and velocity of the content we'll see from our iconic franchises, including GTA, will look dramatically different over the next decade." It's a vague comment, but assumedly the work done on the engine and backend of GTA 6 means we'll see more content arriving in shorter order than we're used to for the series. This is per an article published by IGN in line with the earning's call going live.

Elsewhere in the earnings call, Take-Two referred to its current setup with its mobile, sports, 'core new IP' and 'core existing IP' as "the strongest development pipeline in the company's history". In terms of new IP, Zelnick directed investors to consider the launches of incoming projects like Ken Levine's mysterious Judas and Project Ethos (which we don't know too much about yet, other than it's billed as a "roguelike hero shooter"). For core IP, 8 sequels and 7 remakes, remasters, and platform extensions.

Buoyed by these plans, Zelnick outlines that he believes that fiscal year 2027 "will be a historic year for Take-Two" as the company is buoyed by "recent and upcoming releases". No prizes for what that's referring to. If you're curious about what sort of numbers we may be looking at here, all you need to do is cast your mind back to 2014, where you will remember GTA 5 made $1bn in just three days.

The latest Zelda game is "off to a great start," says Nintendo president Shuntaro Furukawa

Nintendo says The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake is "off to a great start" and the 40th Anniversary Edition Switch 2 console has also been "very positive," heading off speculation from an investor that price hikes may be hurting momentum.

Taking questions as part of its latest financial briefing, Nintendo president Shuntaro Furukawa is pressed on how well the Switch 2 is selling its wares after the console's price jumped to $500 earlier this year. Investors reckon things are slowing down, and they don't like that. As such, one asks the Nintendo suits whether they think current financial goals will still be met.

The short answer is absolutely; just look at how well Zelda's Ocarina of Time remake and 40th-anniversary console are doing.

"Adoption has progressed smoothly over the roughly one and a half years since Nintendo Switch 2 launched last June, and the installed base now exceeds 25 million units," Furukawa says. "At the end of last year's holiday season, we explained that there were regional differences in how well our expectations were met. But the March release of Pokemon Pokopia acted as a driver of global hardware sales, and we entered the new fiscal year with good momentum."

Furukawa continues by saying that, while the Switch 2 did indeed increase in price, the impact hasn't been too great because most people were given plenty of notice and have had plenty of hardware and software bundles to compensate for it.

That takes us to today, where Nintendo is seemingly riding high thanks to all things Zelda. Furukawa says the special version of the Switch 2 designed to celebrate Zelda's 40th anniversary has been "very positive" for the company and has "contributed to strong sales in various regions." Meanwhile, while it's too early to delve too far into the Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake numbers, Furukawa says it's "off to a great start," and that Nintendo is in "good shape for the coming holiday season," too.

"Holiday season sales significantly impact the number of units shipped annually for our dedicated video game platform business," he says. "Given the hardware price revisions, we think the sales trends over the next several weeks will be key to achieving our sales guidance."

Sign up to our Switch 2 Spotlight newsletter to make sure you get the very latest news on Nintendo's new console and its games every week

While no official numbers are given, there are signs that, yeah, those Zelda products are shifting units. As per Circana, the Zelda 40th Anniversary Switch 2 drove record sales for Nintendo in the US. In fact, it was only last month that a Nintendo exec said those at the house of Mario "underestimated" how well it would sell. Stock has been an issue, though a welcome one.

We have less to go on with the Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake. That said, analyst firms say the N64 throwback is the largest physical launch in the UK so far this year. With the festive period coming up, I can see why Nintendo isn't sweating this one too hard right now.

Nintendo "bearing" Switch 2 manufacturing costs to avoid price hikes – but that may have to change if "we cannot absorb the costs through our own efforts."

Ken Jennings isn't going anywhere as Jeopardy!'s host, but he has two famous names he's considered should he need a substitute for a day. Fans may not be surprised to hear that both of these TV personalities have been working hard amid the 2026 TV schedule. These two stars sound like entries on a wishlist, but now that Jennings has put it out there, I'd love to see both of them host the quiz series.

Jennings finally accepted the full-time hosting gig in 2023 in the aftermath of Alex Trebek's passing and various inquiries from curious fans. During a taping, Jennings was asked who'd be a fitting replacement for him in the event he has to miss shows. The first name he floated was none other than longtime Survivor host Jeff Probst. As Jennings astutely mentioned, before Probst was watching contestants battle it out in Fiji, he had a very different gig:

Well, you know who has a lot of Jeopardy! hosting experience is Jeff Probst, who hosted Rock & Roll Jeopardy! back before he was Jeff Probst. I mean, he now hosts three seasons of Survivor a year, I think, so the guy is probably busy.

Probst actually hosts two seasons of Survivor a year, both of which are filmed back-to-back in Fiji in a little under two months. As the host told Variety back in 2024, however, hosting the series is a year-round job. When he's not on the island, he's helping work on post-production, overseeing the casting process for future seasons and hosting a podcast. All this to say, he may be just as busy asJennings suggested, even if he doesn't have a third season to film.

One could argue that in the event that Probst was unavailable, Pop Culture Jeopardy! host Colin Jost could serve as a substitute. Unfortunately, for Jost, though, Jennings named-dropped the host of another hit reality TV series instead.

If Jeff Probst is too tied up in Survivor, Ken Jennings also floated RuPaul as a potential fill-in. The Drag Race host may not be any less busy than Probst, but that didn't stop the former Jeopardy! champ from name-dropping him as well:

Also, RuPaul, I think, would be pretty good.

RuPaul hasn't hosted Jeopardy or a spinoff, but all that Drag Race experience and his time mentoring many successful drag winners has to count for something. I think he'd be a great choice for a one-off, provided he has the time to commit.

It's interesting to hear Ken Jennings not mention Mayim Bialik, as she co-hosted with him for years before he become the sole host. Perhaps he's privy to some info that she's not willing to return to Jeopardy, or he just thought that would be a boring answer to give to the audience. We can only speculate.

For now, it's a non-issue. Ken Jennings is solidly in the role as host, despite pushing off full-time hosting duties for years. It's kind of hilarious, considering everyone, including Alex Trebek, assumed he'd end up in the role, and that he ultimately embraced his fate years later.

Jeopardy! airs on weekdays in syndication, so check their local listings for when and where to watch it. We'll also keep an eye out to see who may substitute for Ken Jennings should he need a day off in the near future, and if Jeff or Ru end up getting tapped for it.

#3764. As investors ask about GTA 6 and AI, Take-Two CEO once again puts faith in dev creativity, states making hit games "remains the purview of human beings"

"Making a big hit was hard then, and it's hard now, and it's going to be hard in the future."

Today, as part of Take-Two Interactive Software's Q2 2027 earnings call, Strauss Zelnick fielded questions from investors after presenting the financial results of the company. One caller was concerned about AI - specifically about the proliferation of AI-powered compilations and decompilations that have been raising piracy concerns for publishers over the past few weeks.

Zelnick notes that "[the video games] business has been largely immune to piracy" thanks to factors like file size, how console ecosystems work, and aspects related to the online nature of the games industry. That said, Strauss continues, there is a threat posed to the industry because of AI. However, he assures listening investors that Take-Two is appropriately scaling its measures against bad faith actors using artificial intelligence.

"We are utterly focused on enhancing our technical defences and enhancing our legal activities appropriately. And - at the same time, without in any way being cavalier - every entertainment business that exists is subject to some element of piracy, [and] this is likely to invade our business to a greater or lesser extent. I think it will be manageable and we are focused on it."

Zelnick pivots back to AI again later in the call, where one investor once again asks about AI, seemingly keen to learn whether the CEO feels it can provide GTA 6 developer Rockstar with any kind of "competitive advantage" in the games industry. Given Zelnick's previous comments on the subject, his answer was not a complete surprise.

"It's always been true [that technology benefits us]," explains Zelnick. "We've always created our entertainment inside computers with technology. All advances have benefited us, and I don't expect that that will change - in fact, I hope it'll accelerate. I think at the same time, what we're known for [at Take-Two] is the desire to make the best entertainment on Earth. And, more often than not, we have succeeded - and the creativity that drives that success is human creativity harnessing technology. And I think that's what you'll see in the future, too.

"Undoubtedly some of the most recent technological advances that you've seen have made it easier to create assets. Where all that is consistent with the story of our business. When I started in interactive entertainment (longer ago than I would like to say), it was really difficult to create an asset in a computer. Today, it's a whole lot easier - but you know what's not easier? Making a big hit. Making a big hit was hard then, and it's hard now, and it's going to be hard in the future. And hit creation remains the purview of human beings."

This isn't the first instance of AI skepticism we've seen from Strauss Zelnick. Back in March, he outright rejected the idea that AI can tackle games on the scale of GTA 6. Elsewhere in the call, the Take-Two CEO reiterated how well GTA 6 is tracking as he reasserted pre-order numbers are well above expectations, and promised that the success of the game will "set a new baseline" for Take-Two's gaming business.

The suite of GFX13 patches aren't particularly exciting in themselves, but they do suggest there might actually be some new GPUs next year.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

AMD's next-gen graphics architecture has popped up in a graphics driver for the first time, with a suite of GFX13 patches going live in an AMDGPU Linux kernel graphics driver. This has first been reported by Michael Larabel at Phoronix, who spotted a series of eight patches being posted by AMDGPU maintainer, Alex Deucher.

The RDNA 4 GPUs, the Radeon RX 9070 XT et al, were all noted under the GFX12 codename in previous patches, so it is only natural to expect that GFX13 refers to the next generation of AMD graphics cards featuring the RDNA 5 architecture.

The timing of these graphics driver patches would suggest support for the new GPUs is going into the upcoming Linux 7.5 kernel release. With Linux 7.0 dropping earlier this year, and the 7.4 version currently in release candidate testing at the moment, it is expected that the 7.5 kernel release will occur sometime in early 2027.

Wee side note for you... that's not the only interesting thing happening in Linux 7.5, however, as it will also mark the end of an era for Intel. The multimedia extensions it introduced in the Pentium era with MMX will have their last vestiges of optimisations removed in the upcoming kernel release.

At the moment, the current expectation on the actual AMD GPU release schedule itself would see one mid-range RDNA 5 card coming out in 2027, using silicon under yet another codename: AT2. That would tally neatly with the architecture's appearance in this new Linux kernel.

As for the actual code that's been dropped in this series of driver patches… it's not particularly exciting. There is a lot of code, and I am absolutely not smart nor Linux-savvy enough enough to be able to discern anything special from them, but Larabel has himself noted that as far as he can tell there isn't anything in there that reveals tasty new tidbits about the potential future RDNA 5 feature set.

But that's not to say further patches won't do that, so it will be worth keeping an eye on these updates going forward as potentially more functionality-based patches get dropped into the upcoming kernel.

#3762. Switch 2 and Switch consoles updated to version 23.5.0 as Nintendo quietly re-introduces eShop gifting

Nintendo has just pushed out a new update to all Switch and Switch 2 consoles, bringing the firmware on both up to version 23.5.0. The headline change with the new update is support and compatibility for an upcoming update that will allow members of a Nintendo Account family group to gift games to one another.

The feature itself is expected to go live on 17th November, 2026. "Just in time for the holidays, a new feature will let family group members gift digital games to other members of their group," says a post on a dedicated blog on the Nintendo site. "You will be able to gift digital products that you purchase through Nintendo eShop on your device to family group members. This includes eligible games as well as DLC and upgrade packs. As a reminder, anyone with a Nintendo Account can easily set up a family group and add members (up to 8 total)."

The publisher notes, however, that "some products may not be eligible for digital gifting" and that "supervised accounts are not able to send digital gifts". Additionally, "the number of digital gift purchases allowed in a given period is limited".

"This feature is a great way to celebrate a special occasion with your kids. Happy gifting!" concludes Nintendo. Just in time for the holidays, how thoughtful. It's worth noting that a previous iteration of this support was included back on the Nintendo Wii, but that was much more robust than this - back then, the publisher allowed users to send WiiWare or Virtual Console games to anyone on their Wii Friend list via the Wii Shop Channel, rather than just those limited to their immediate group. This functionality was lost in 2019, alongside the closure of the Wii Shop Channel.

The patch also came with some other updates, you can see those listed below.

"Creating new and unique products is our top priority"

A Nintendo exec has stressed the importance of creating the company's signature experiences with the rise of AI development.

During a recent investors' meeting attended by multiple Nintendo employees, a question was asked about the company's emphasis on game quality, noting that this, in turn, "seems to be lengthening the development period for each title." The question then poses how Nintendo plans to balance creativity with business management.

Yusuke Beppu, senior executive officer and corporate director for Nintendo, responds, "Development is the engine of Nintendo's competitiveness and value. Creating new and unique products is our top priority," adding that "balancing creativity and business is always challenging." Beppu continues, "Unless we satisfy consumers, our efforts will not lead us to good business results."

Beppu goes on to say that "technologies like the internet and AI have dramatically increased the amount of digital content available to the world," noting the sheer amount of free entertainment available. He also says "we are conducting business in an environment that is different from the past," and that given this increased competition, "it is important to offer unique entertainment experiences that are very Nintendo, so that consumers will choose Nintendo."

With the question itself about Nintendo's lengthy development periods, it's worth noting that Nintendo has been releasing games pretty much every month since the Nintendo Switch 2 launched, sometimes multiple, compared to the likes of Sony and Xbox; I'd say that's pretty fast. With or without AI.

Could a remade Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time be exciting enough to revitalise Switch 2 hardware sales? That was the big question. And early sales figures suggest the answer is yes, it can.

The Switch 2, which had been declining in hardware sales over the last few months, just had its highest (dollar) sales week of 2026 in the US so far following the game's release, according to Circana analyst Mat Piscatella on Bluesky.

The accompanying Legend of Zelda: 40th Anniversary Edition console in particular is responsible for a notable jump in Switch 2 hardware dollar sales. The themed, special edition console has been popular, with various retailers immediately running out of stock and a rise in scalping.

It's worth noting that The Legend of Zelda: 40th Anniversary Edition console, priced $520 / £430, does not include a copy of the game. Also, because the console was released 29th October, and the Ocarina of Time remake on 5th November, their sales results will come in separate monthly reports.

The Ocarina of Time launch also caused US hardware spending to jump by 81 percent during the week ending 31st October compared to the same period last year.

Christian Donlan awarded The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time a glitzy five stars in Eurogamer's review, writing: "This is Ocarina as it's always been, as timeless and intricate, but it also has a vibrancy and clarity that makes it feel like it was just created last Wednesday."

Even the brightest stars hit career lows.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Ones of Matt Damon’s 2026 movie releases, The Odyssey, couldn’t stop breaking records after its debut this past July. It became the second highest-grossing movie of the year with a worldwide haul of $1.8 billion. It's also the highest-grossing R-rated movie ever and the 11th highest-grossing movie ever. At present, Damon's name is also being mentioned amid awards season conversations. Still, as the star comes off his big year, he's speaking honestly about what he considers to be the low points of his career.

The Good Will Hunting star was recently asked when he knew The Odyssey would be a hit, and he admitted that moment came when he saw the movie for himself. Decades earlier, Damon had those same instincts, as he explained to GQ. However, in those cases, the results weren't nearly as strong as they are now. While discussing one particular slump, Damon named one of the films he had on the docket in 2000:

The first time was before The Bourne Identity came out. I had done The Legend of Bagger Vance with Will [Smith] and Charlize [Theron], and that movie didn’t do well. And Will was, as he is now, the biggest star. And so it’s like, it’s not Will’s fault. [Laughs]

While The Legend of Bagger Vance may have had one of the best golf scenes in Hollywood history, it was definitely a box office bomb, grossing $39.5 million globally against a reported production budget of $80 million. Not to mention, the sports-drama film has low critics' score of 43% on Rotten Tomatoes. In the long run, it didn't hurt the careers of Damon, Smith or Theron, but I can understand why the Bourne star would've been shaken by the reception at that time.

Damon, unfortunately, experienced another setback after the release of Bagger Vance. There's another failed movie of Damon's that he's still not over, and it was released in 2000 as well:

And then I did All the Pretty Horses with Billy Bob [Thornton], and that was a whole fraught experience. There were different ideas between the studio and between Billy Bob about what the movie should be, and so it ended up getting cut in a way that wasn’t to Billy’s liking and it didn’t do well. And so I had had these misses. And so there was this stretch where the phone just didn’t ring. The silence was…. It was a real rose-colored lenses coming off.

I can imagine how frustrating that must have been to envision what you wanted your movie to be, only for the studio to take over. With that, it's hard not to wonder what could have been if Billy Bob Thornton had had his way. Ultimately, All the Pretty Horses was another bomb for Damon, as it made only $18.1 million worldwide on a budget of $57 million. As for its critics score on Rotten Tomatoes, it's at 33%, as of this writing.

Considering the Saving Private Ryan star's immense success, it's now somewhat wild to think about Damon worrying about his acting career, but it happens. He'd later experience a huge lull with no job offers, until Steven Soderbergh approached him about The Informant! The Ocean’s alum was so happy that he even offered to write the screenplay. While Scott Z. Burns ended up with the screenwriter role, Damon was still honored to be offered this leading role after a long career stretch.

It's so refreshing that Matt Damon has no problem looking back on the rougher points of his career. It’s also not unheard of for actors to look down on their own movies, but Damon speaks more diplomatically about Bagger Vance and All the Pretty Horses. I can imagine setbacks being hard to think about, but I get the sense that they've served as fuel for his career. And just look at him now. He's the lead of one of the biggest movies of all time and could even land himself some awards over the next few months.

On that note, The Odyssey is now available now available to rent on various digital platforms.

Just your average South Floridian cinephile who believes the pen is mightier than the sword.

Valve opens up the doors to the data it's been collecting.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

The Steam Deck is the most popular handheld gaming PC, and no doubt a lot of you own one already. It's also far from the most powerful handheld on the market, meaning devs have to get optimisation just right to allow the Deck to maintain 60 or even 30 fps. Now, Valve is letting everyone see exactly how well those optimisations are made by listing average Steam Deck frame rate data on game store pages.

Valve explains that this applies to any game that's been tested for Steam Deck compatibility, not just Verified ones. It applies to 'Verified', 'Playable', and 'Unsupported' ones. Apparently that means thousands of games right now.

The data is based on what different users have opted in to provide, which, despite only being for opt-inners, presumably still gives a big sample size. We've known about Valve collecting this kind of data since at least February this year, and we heard about Valve handing it over to game devs just last month.

Now, Valve is letting us all get in on the action. To look at a game's average frame rate data, go to its store page, look on the right-hand side for where it lists its 'Steam Deck Compatibility', and click 'Learn more'.

Once there, you're shown the average fps, and if you click the down arrow, you can view a "framerate histogram... breaking down the percentage of data samples at each framerate." The bigger a particular bar, the more of the game session (on average) is enjoyed at that frame rate.

I checked the Elden Ring data, for instance, and found that the Steam Deck OLED averages 42 fps and the Steam Deck LCD 38 fps. The latter seems mostly split between 60 fps and 30 fps, with most at 30 and little in between, leading me to believe most players lock their frame rate for more stable gameplay.

The biggest benefit, though, will probably just be the ability to quickly view the average frame rate. It will mean less guessing exactly how well a game should perform on your Steam Deck before you decide to purchase. And that can benefit other handheld gamers, too, as if you have a more powerful handheld, you'll know you can achieve at least that frame rate or higher.

#3757. Under pressure, Big Walk studio reveals it used generative AI "sparingly" while making its hit 2026 game

"It has become a matter of public interest."

Australian developer House House has revealed it used generative AI "sparingly" to help make celebrated, indie, multiplayer puzzle game Big Walk.

In a statement sent to Aftermath - following a judging fallout related to the Independent Games Festival - House House revealed it had used large language models primarily to help debug the game's code.

"In the final stretch of Big Walk's development, LLMs were used sparingly by House House to help work through difficult technical challenges and bugs," the developer said. "In some cases, snippets from LLM responses were copied as a starting point to be modified into game code - we'd estimate that well under 0.1 percent of Big Walk's code had anything to do with this usage, and generative AI was not used in any other context when making the game."

House House added: "The primary use case for House House's use of LLMs was to research, via chatbots, issues we encountered with third-party code."

The studio's revelation comes after a sizeable number of IGF jurors - 19 of them - issued a statement saying they would not vote for any game that used generative AI during its development. This was done after seeing "a significant increase" in entry submissions involving generative AI use, which "set off some fairly intense discussion and disagreement across the judge and jury pools". And rather than not vote for these in silence, a collection of jurors decided to take a public stand.

House House hadn't disclosed Big Walk generative AI use anywhere before disclosing it for its IGF submission. "We have not made any disclosure on Steam as the platform does not request disclosure of code or chatbot usage," the studio explained. "We are posting this disclosure as it has become a matter of public interest."

House House added: "This is not an endorsement of, or argument for, the use of AI tools, however minimal. We have some concern that voluntary disclosures like this might contribute to the normalisation of this technology, or its treatment as 'inevitable'. We support the work of those who are trying to limit the harm generative AI is doing to video games and our world, and apologise that Big Walk's LLM usage may not meet their standards.

"Big Walk was developed without an internal AI usage policy in place, and we consider that lack of policy a failure. We will work to have a more comprehensive policy going forwards."

It's a revelation that's likely to leave a taint of some degree on one of this year's brightest stars - a game Eurogamer awarded a full five stars to in its Big Walk review.
